entities.summary:
Harvard University, founded in 1636 in Cambridge, Massachusetts, is the oldest university in the United States and one of the most prestigious in the world. With an endowment exceeding $50 billion — the world's largest — Harvard has produced 162 Nobel laureates, 8 US presidents, and 32 heads of state, making it the most consequential single educational institution in modern history.

Founded just six years after the Massachusetts Bay Colony's establishment as Harvard College, the institution was named after its first major benefactor, clergyman John Harvard, who donated half his estate and his 400-volume library in 1638. Originally training Puritan ministers, Harvard evolved into a comprehensive research university whose graduate schools in law, medicine, business, and government have trained generations of global leaders.

Harvard Business School's MBA program, founded in 1908, created the modern business school model; Harvard Law School trained three of nine current Supreme Court Justices; Harvard Kennedy School shapes global governance policy. The university's Cambridge campus and Massachusetts Hall (1720), the oldest surviving university building in North America, anchor America's most prestigious academic cluster. Harvard's decision to remain selective has been challenged by lawsuits over affirmative action (Students for Fair Admissions v. Harvard, 2023) in which the Supreme Court ruled race-conscious admissions unconstitutional.
